extracted.intended_audience: machine-learning researchers and developers building/evaluating video question-answering and video-reasoning models (especially for surprising/funny/creative/magic videos)
extracted.subtask_description: A VideoQA benchmark for surprising videos (humor, creative performance, magic) that evaluates models on counter-intuitive timestamp localization, detailed video description, reasoning about counter-intuitiveness, plus higher-level tasks like title attribution and creativity scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive timestamp localization
rubrics_metrics.description: Counter-intuitive timestamp localization (one of three common tasks associated with each subset; see H1-3, C1-3, M1-3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task: localize the timestamp(s) in the video corresponding to the counter-intuitive or surprising event. The benchmark establishes rigorous QA tasks designed to assess the model's capability in counter-intuitive timestamp localization across HumorQA, CreativeQA, and MagicQA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed video description
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed video description (one of three common tasks associated with each subset; see H1-3, C1-3, M1-3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task: generate a detailed description of the video content. The dataset's QA pairs include free-text descriptions intended to evaluate models' ability in producing rich, accurate, and relevant video descriptions for surprising content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning around counter-intuitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasoning around counter-intuitiveness (one of three common tasks associated with each subset; see H1-3, C1-3, M1-3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task: produce reasoning that explains why the event is counter-intuitive or surprising. The benchmark assesses model capability in reasoning about counter-intuitiveness, including explanation and inference about unexpected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-level task: attributing a fitting and vivid title
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributing a fitting and vivid title to the video (higher-level task for HumorQA and CreativeQA; referenced as H4, C4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task: assign a concise, vivid, and fitting title for HumorQA and CreativeQA clips. This evaluates higher-level summarization/creative-labeling ability beyond factual description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-level task: scoring video creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring the video creativity (higher-level task mentioned for the benchmark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task: produce a creativity score or assessment for the video. The benchmark poses this as a higher-level evaluation to measure subjective/creative judgment by models.

rubrics_metrics.name: FunQA Multi-choice Dataset format
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA Multi-choice Dataset: QA pairs in multiple-choice form intended for training and testing arbitrary models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format details: 'in this dataset our QA pairs are in the form of multiple choice, the answer is a word, phrase, or short sentence, and the type of questions are all descriptions.' Use this format when training models expecting fixed-choice labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: FunQA Dialog Dataset format
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA Dialog Dataset: QA pairs converted into recursive dialogues with added context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creation details: 'Most of the current LLMs are in the form of dialogues. To cater to their data input, we produced the FunQA Dialog dataset, in which we used GPT-3.5 to convert QA pairs into recursive dialogues with added context.' Use for evaluating dialogue-style LLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation tooling and recommended automatic metric (BLEURT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation uses provided code (classic_eval.py, gpt4_eval.py) and recommends BLEURT for automated evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: install bleurt, download the recommended checkpoint (BLEURT-20), and run provided scripts (./scripts/run_classic_eval.sh and ./scripts/run_gpt4_eval.sh). The repo includes evaluation code for model outputs (JSON). The README also indicates an evaluation pipeline involving GPT-4 for additional evaluation (gpt4_eval.py).

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted reasoning capabilities to measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark aims to reveal model weaknesses across spatial-temporal reasoning, visual-centered reasoning, and free-text generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the dataset and evaluation tasks to measure performance gaps in: spatial-temporal reasoning (understanding events across time/space), visual-centered reasoning (inferring from visual cues), and free-text generation (quality of open-ended answers). The README reports significant performance gaps in these areas for existing VideoQA models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset scale and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset size and composition as a usage/coverage criterion: 312K free-text QA pairs derived from 4.3K video clips spanning 24 video hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: benchmark coverage and statistical power are determined by 312K QA pairs from 4.3K clips. Includes three subsets (HumorQA, CreativeQA, MagicQA). Users should download train/val/test zips and annotation JSON files (FunQA_train.json, FunQA_val.json, FunQA_test.json).
